The Intermediate Value Theorem guarantees that if a function \( f \) is continuous on \([a, b]\) and \( N \) lies between \( f(a) \) and \( f(b) \), then there exists some \( c \) in \([a, b]\) such that \( f(c) = N \) [1].

The sign stays the same on both sides of \( x = 1 \) because \( (x-1)^2 \) is always positive, and \( x+2 \) remains positive for values of \( x \) near 1. Thus, the denominator is always positive, and the negative numerator keeps the whole expression negative [1].
